summary.text: Case 1 was a patient aged up to 30 years with a history of hospitalization for mania 10 years earlier. After a first pregnancy during which she was well, she was admitted within 1 week post-partum with mania and psychotic symptoms, and the first admission lasted about 2 weeks.
The first 24-hour actigraphy recording on day 6 of the admission, taken on olanzapine and oxazepam, showed a high mean activity level and a short, disrupted nocturnal sleep interval of about 5 h.

About 1 month later she was readmitted with a severe relapse of the manic episode and more marked psychotic symptoms; medication changed to quetiapine, clonazepam and zopiclone, and the 6-week admission included a recording on its 4th day with a lower mean activity level, longer sleep, more daytime rest-activity shifts and higher sample entropy peaks than R1.

summary.text: Case 2 was a patient aged about 55 years with bipolar I disorder who was hospitalized five times within 3 months for a fluctuating mixed episode. History included psychotic symptoms with auditory hallucinations, more than 10 hospitalizations including an involuntary one for severe mania, and no important alcohol or substance use or major physical illness.

Three hospitalizations included 24-hour actigraphy (R1, R2, R3) on the third, second and second day of admission, on valproate 1500 mg, oxazepam 25 mg and quetiapine 600, 200 and 500 mg. The recordings showed consistent patterns with similar mean activity; during R2 the patient had visual hallucinations and paranoid delusions, and the text also reports greater daytime inactivity with higher sample entropy peaks and reported symptom fluctuations over 24 h.

summary.text: Case 3 was a patient aged between 60 and 65 years with a 40-year history of bipolar disorder, prior alcohol misuse, suicidal ideation and self-harm, and a good response to lithium although relapses often followed small dose modifications. The patient was initially admitted in a depressive episode.

The first recording on day 2 of the admission was on quetiapine 275 mg and lithium 210 mg and showed motor activity interspersed with frequent rest periods, low sample entropy and afternoon sample entropy peaks. Because of renal complications of lithium, the regimen was changed to quetiapine and lamotrigine during the admission, which lasted about 6 weeks until remission.

Within 2 weeks the patient was readmitted with mania and intermittent psychotic symptoms. The second recording on day 2, on lamotrigine 200 mg, quetiapine 500 mg and single doses of oxazepam and alimemazine, showed higher mean activity and elevated sample entropy. The patient improved gradually and was discharged after 10 weeks.
